title: Behavioral Anchors
hook: Willpower never got me to journal. Doing it right after my first coffee did.
statement: Tie new habits to things you already do every day. The trigger does the remembering for you.
explainer: Motivation comes and goes. An existing routine shows up every day no matter what. Hook the new habit onto it and it starts running on autopilot.
sop: List 3 habits you keep failing to stick to.
For each, pick a daily action that already happens like clockwork.
Do the new habit right after that Trigger, same time and place.
Rate each Trigger from 1 to 10 and count your Repetition for 14 days.
Once it's automatic, stack the next habit on top.
equation_example: Trigger reliability 8, Repetition 6 times this week. 8 × 6 = 48. Higher means the habit is turning automatic. Lower means the anchor is weak or you're skipping too often.
question: Pick one thing you do every morning without thinking and attach a new habit to it.
closing_statement: Automatic beats motivated, every single time.
